cases.assertion: authenticated status response matches schema and content type
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: zero-byte artifact round-trips exactly
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: small binary artifact round-trips exactly
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: Content-Length and octet-stream requirements are enforced or correctly accepted
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: duration round-trips; absent duration becomes zero; malformed duration is attributable
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: tag, SHA, and dirty-hash preservation are scored separately
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: absence is optional; an implemented route matches the documented map
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: absence is optional; an implemented route accepts the documented event shape
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: documented response status and actual client acceptance are separate verdicts
cases.reason: The wire runner records the documented upload status; client acceptance is scored only by native runs.

cases.assertion: genuine 404 is distinguishable from every fail-soft error class
cases.reason: The wire runner separates a genuine 404 from fault classes; client fail-soft and log evidence stay native/lab.

cases.assertion: missing, malformed, unknown, read, and write bearer cases follow the policy matrix
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: read bearer cannot PUT and reader execution role cannot write storage
cases.reason: The wire runner covers the bearer half; the reader execution role's storage denial needs deployed IAM (lab).

cases.assertion: writer cannot be invoked outside the authorized gateway path
cases.reason: Direct writer invocation outside the gateway needs the deployed Lambda/IAM boundary.

cases.assertion: a valid bearer cannot select or retrieve another namespace
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: empty, conflicting, traversal-like, encoded, and oversized selectors fail closed
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: invalid, traversal-like, encoded, empty, and oversized hashes fail closed
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: valid Turbo HMAC tag is preserved and accepted by the producing client epoch
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy.

cases.assertion: signed client rejects a response with no tag and direct receipt identifies the cause
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy.

cases.assertion: signed client rejects a modified tag without materializing outputs
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy.

cases.assertion: signed client rejects modified bytes without materializing outputs
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy.

cases.assertion: tag produced for another team identity is rejected
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy. The wrong-team response is replayed by the fault proxy, so it scores clients only; backend tenant isolation is RC-014.

cases.assertion: old and new namespace epochs do not silently cross-restore or downgrade to unsigned
cases.reason: Requires the exact pinned Turbo executables and signing epochs; executed by cache conformance-native through the fault proxy.

cases.assertion: 401, 403, 429, 5xx, timeout, reset, and truncated body have distinct direct receipts
cases.reason: The wire run covers 401, 403 and a genuine 404; cache conformance-lab injects 429, 503, timeout, reset and truncation at the fault proxy and scores observability.

cases.assertion: failed and ambiguous writes do not produce a success receipt or corrupt a prior object
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: concurrent identical and conflicting writes have a defined atomic result
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: readers observe either the prior complete artifact or the new complete artifact
cases.reason: Reproducible against any target with the direct HTTP runner and per-run random hashes.

cases.assertion: p50, p95, p99, and twice observed p99 sizes complete within declared bounds
cases.reason: cache conformance-lab measures the p50/p95/p99, 2x p99 and observed-max sizes; only a disposable-deployment run is representative.

cases.assertion: observed peak and 1.5 times peak preserve correctness and bounded latency
cases.reason: cache conformance-lab measures observed peak and 1.5x peak read/write concurrency; only a disposable-deployment run is representative.

cases.assertion: expiry and namespace cleanup affect only the intended epoch and remain observable
cases.reason: Retention and namespace cleanup need storage lifecycle timers.

cases.assertion: synthetic bearer, signature key, artifact content, and sensitive paths are absent from logs and traces
cases.reason: Log and trace privacy needs backend log capture.

cases.assertion: client run, task hash, backend request, object operation, and result class correlate without secret or unbounded-cardinality fields
cases.reason: Correlation needs client, backend and storage telemetry capture.

cases.assertion: incumbent endpoint and epoch can be restored from a rehearsed receipt without mixed writes
cases.reason: Cutback needs a rehearsed endpoint and epoch restoration receipt.
